decision.reason: The closure that accepts (openssh-final-close) was not derived against the artefacts of the candidate source. HEAD b004a99d5 rebuilds deterministically to libcrypto be578c86 / libssl c6eddcfe / legacy 43db4443 / openssl 9486da43 (two independent runs each). The receipts' closure artifact is libcrypto c2d73687, which I reproduced only by reverting the four legacy-init source files to 2ff301947. Re-running consumer_closure.py at the HEAD artefact therefore REFUSES on STALE_HASH (libcrypto be578c86 not the inventory's c2d73687; src/evp/legacy_blake2.rs not the V1 source hash at 2ff301947). Independently, at least one of the 28 'contract-bounded' sites is mislabelled: 0x18f440 in ossl_method_construct_this calls mcm->construct, an in-image stack-local table entry (construct_evp_method), not an OSSL_provider_init edge.
decision.primary_failing_element: 1. exact candidate identity match (and consequently 5/6: the dependency closure is not complete at that identity)
other_failing_elements: 2. exact consumer binary identity: the closure analysed ssh c8723f34 / sshd dccccf07; the L7 runtime executed ssh 23c260e9 / sshd d9e92604, and the runtime rows still embed no consumer binary digest

6. every applicable safety obligation discharged: the only adopted site at the HEAD source (OSSH-FC-006, sm3_int_init) is anchored to line 125, which is now a struct field; the live unsafe fn moved to line 181 and is outside the receipt's declared range
7. no unresolved dynamic dispatch or callback edge: one of the 28 contract-bounded sites is an internal in-image callback misclassified under the OSSL_provider_init contract
8. relevant BOUNDARY instruments: only deliberate-failure canaries ran; no instrumented crate suite at be578c86; Loom/Kani/mutation NOT_RUN
9. SEAL requirements: full v1 census regeneration, full forensic regeneration, held-out replay and release-candidate seal NOT_RUN
10. independent review accepted: this independent review does not accept the claim

contract_bounded_site_checks.method: read the cited public contract, then map each site's address in the be578c86 image with addr2line and read the call sequence in the objdump

checked.disassembly: call *%rax, where %rax = MALLOC_FN (0x8a69a0) when non-NULL, else default_malloc
checked.verdict: correctly contract-bounded: this is the CRYPTO_set_mem_functions malloc seam

checked.disassembly: call *%rax, where %rax = FREE_FN (0x8a6998) when non-NULL, else default_free
call *0x28(%rax) where %rax = *(mcm); mcm is the stack-local OsslMethodConstructMethod built in src/evp/fetch.rs:1008 with construct = construct_evp_method
checked.verdict: MISLABELLED: the target is an in-image, statically knowable method-constructor callback; OSSL_provider_init does not establish its precondition. This site is not provider-init shaped

contract_bounded_site_checks.conclusion: the allocator class is sound at the sites checked; the provider class mixes genuine provider dispatch (provider_init) with internal callbacks, so the 28 are not all contract-bounded

switch_bound_verification.method: reconstructed the exact c2d736 image, then read each compiler jump table from the ELF at the cited base and bound, and compared membership against a 16 KiB-entry (64 KiB) over-scan
switch_bound_verification.conclusion: SOUND. Every removed edge lies 30-48 KiB past the compiler's own table bound and outside the real table. The switch-bound correction removed artefacts of the 64 KiB scan, not real targets; narrowing on this basis was justified
